claims.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Stars are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.

claims.head: A tough night ahead for Hughes
claims.call: The Stars’ P1 (Heiskanen and Harley) spends at least 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Devils’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Stars keep sending Heiskanen and Harley out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Glen Gulutzan has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Devils’ first line is Gritsyuk, Hughes and Bratt.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 28% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 7th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 44%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Esa Lindell is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Thomas Harley has taken his spot beside Miro Heiskanen.
Sam Steel is out and has missed the last 2 games. Joel Kiviranta has taken his spot beside Mikko Rantanen and Wyatt Johnston.
Matt Duchene is on long-term injured reserve (abdomen injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Matthew Seminoff was added to the roster on Oct 26 and has played beside Colin Blackwell and Justin Hryckowian.
Dylan Hryckowian was added to the roster on Oct 26 and has played beside Jamie Benn and Arttu Hyry.

DAL.head: A slightly uphill night for the Stars
DAL.body: Even though Dallas has home-ice advantage, the Stars will be without Lindell, and New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Stars can tip it if their power play gets going.

NJD.head: Leaning the Devils’ way
NJD.body: Even though Dallas has home-ice advantage, the Stars will be without Lindell, and New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Stars can still swing it if their power play gets going.

story.head: The Stars are rolling
paras: The Stars are on a tear, five straight wins. The Devils have won three straight.

It’s strength against strength: the Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Stars are one of the best at the penalty kill. At home, Glen Gulutzan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Devils’ first line.
